# src/modules/accounting/services/gl/reclassification

## Purpose

Move posted amounts from one GL account to another, as one reversible batch.
Behind `propose_reclassification` (read) and `post_reclassification_batch`
(write) in `src/lib/mcp/tools/`.

## The constraint the whole module is built around

**A reclassification NEVER mutates a posted line.** For each source line it posts
a PAIR — a contra on the source account and the same amount re-applied to the
target — and leaves the original exactly as posted.

```
original   DR 49775627 Unallocated Expense   1,000
contra     CR 49775627 Unallocated Expense   1,000
applied    DR 5100     Materials & Supplies  1,000
```

`UPDATE gl_journal_lines SET gl_account_id = …` produces the same closing
balances and destroys three things: a trial balance somebody signed stops
reproducing, the original classification is gone from the audit trail, and there
is nothing to reverse — the reclassification itself becomes invisible. The pair
IS the record that it happened, and it is what makes the batch undoable through
the ordinary `reverse_journal_entry` path rather than through a bespoke un-edit.

Nothing in this directory issues an UPDATE or a DELETE against
`gl_journal_lines`. If a change here wants to, that is the signal to stop.

The mirror is direction-agnostic by construction (the contra swaps debit and
credit), so a credit-balance move needs no branch and cannot get one wrong.

## Caller contract

- `plan.ts#planReclassification` is the ONE entry point for both tools, and is
  entirely READ-ONLY. That is what makes the dry run honest: every row-state
  guard the live path runs has already run before the two diverge, and only the
  write itself is skipped.
- `post.ts#postReclassBatch` is the only writer. It has no try/catch anywhere:
  `registry.call()` gives a write tool ONE savepoint which unwinds on a THROW,
  so any `catch → toolError` after the first write would RELEASE it and let the
  transport commit a half-moved account.
- A REFUSAL is about the REQUEST (`ReclassRefusal`, rendered as a pre-write
  `toolError`); a SKIP is about the DATA (`ReclassSkip`, one line, never costing
  the rest of the batch).
- `company_id` is on every query. `gl_journal_lines` has no composite
  `(id, company_id)` key, so an id-only lookup would read across tenants.

## Main signatures

```typescript
// plan.ts
planReclassification(input: ReclassPlanInput): Promise<ReclassPlan | ReclassRefusal>
MAX_RECLASS_LINES = 500   // refuse above it; never truncate silently
// candidates.ts — queries only
findReclassCandidates(companyId, q): Promise<CandidateRow[]>   // LIMIT limit + 1
countReclassCandidates(companyId, q): Promise<number>          // the universe, own COUNT
// partition.ts — the decision, PURE (re-exported from candidates.ts)
partitionCandidates(rows, opts): { movable, skipped }
// lineLock.ts
lockReclassLinesForUpdate(companyId, lineIds): Promise<string[]>  // ids actually locked
// journals.ts
buildReclassJournals(lines, sourceId, targetId, names, postingDate): ReclassJournalDraft[]  // PURE
// impact.ts
computeReclassImpact(input): Promise<ReclassImpact>
// post.ts
postReclassBatch(companyId, userId, input): Promise<PostedReclassBatch>
// batchService.ts
createReclassBatch / recordReclassBatchLines / getReclassBatch
```

## Business rules

- **Skip reasons**, machine-stable, in the order they are reported:
  `entry_reversed`, `entry_is_reversal`, `reclassification_contra`,
  `appeared_after_lock`, `already_reclassified`, `zero_amount`,
  `unreproducible_analysis_coding`,
  `unknown_vat_type`, `vat_period_locked`, `source_period_missing`,
  `source_period_closed`.
- **A REVERSAL IS A PAIR, AND BOTH HALVES ARE SKIPPED.** `reversed_at` marks the
  entry that WAS reversed; `reversal_of_id` marks the entry that DID the
  reversing. They mirror each other line for line on the same account and
  together net to zero. Guarding on `reversed_at` alone tears the pair in half:
  the original charge stays on the source and its cancellation is carried to the
  target, and NEITHER account nets to zero afterwards. That defect shipped in
  the first cut of this module and was invisible to every safety surface it
  built — the before/after P&L is band-level, both accounts sat in the same
  band, so `no_profit_and_loss_effect` fired and read as reassurance. Verified
  live: 39 lines / R15,477,616.91 on `49775626` and 5 lines / R407,422.11 on
  `49775627`. Both halves skip rather than both moving, because the pair
  contributes nothing to any balance — moving it posts two more journals to
  relocate a nil, and reclassifying a reversed charge is a different intent from
  reclassifying a live one.
- **READ → LOCK → RE-READ, on the write path only** (`lineLock.ts`). Nothing
  else serialises two DIFFERENT requests over the same lines: the registry's
  idempotency lock keys on the key, all three duplicate-move guards are
  read-committed reads of rows the peer has not committed, and the
  `(batch_id, source_line_id)` unique index is per BATCH so two batch ids cannot
  collide. Two batches under different keys would otherwise both post the same
  R11.3m.
  **The lock alone fixes nothing.** Held only across the INSERT, both batches
  would still have DECIDED on stale reads. So: read to learn the ids, `FOR
  UPDATE` them, then read AGAIN and evaluate every row-state guard on that
  second read — by which time the peer's batch rows are committed and its lines
  report as `already_reclassified`.
  `FOR UPDATE`, not an advisory lock, and on the LINES, not the account: this is
  `bankTxLock.ts`'s pattern, which the repo added after a double-post got
  through the same way, and the contended resource genuinely is the set of lines
  — two batches can only double-move a line they BOTH selected. Two batches over
  non-overlapping windows do not conflict and are not made to wait.
  `ORDER BY jl.id … FOR UPDATE` acquires in ascending id order (Postgres puts
  `LockRows` above `Sort`; verified across index, bitmap and seq plans), so
  overlapping batches queue rather than deadlock — the same total-order argument
  `writeBankBulkAllocate` makes, in one round trip instead of 500.
  A line that appears between the lock and the re-read is NOT locked, so it is
  skipped as `appeared_after_lock` rather than moved — and skipped rather than
  dropped, so it stays inside `rowsTotal + excluded === universeTotal`.
  A preview takes no lock: holding locks on hundreds of posted lines for the
  length of a read would block every real batch on them for no benefit.
- **A VAT control account is refused as source or target.** `vatReturnService`
  decides VAT201 membership by `account_subtype IN ('vat_input','vat_output',
  'tax')`, and a line landing on one with a NULL `vat_type` is swept into box 15
  at full value. A warning an agent can ignore is not a control on a SARS
  submission. `'tax'` is in the set even though it is not VAT (FINDINGS B37)
  because the return reads it as VAT today.
- **Every dimension the source line carries goes onto BOTH legs** —
  `project_id`, `cost_center_id`, `vat_type`, `bu_id`. `cc1_id` / `cc2_id`
  cannot be expressed by `JournalLineInput` at all, so a line carrying either is
  SKIPPED rather than posted with them dropped; zero production lines carry them
  today. An unrecognised `vat_type` (the column is bare `text` with no CHECK)
  skips for the same reason.
- **Periods.** With no `posting_date`, one journal per distinct source entry
  date — period-neutral, and every line whose own period is CLOSED is skipped
  because a closed period cannot be posted into. With a `posting_date`, ONE
  journal on that day; nothing is skipped for a closed source period, and the
  charge moves between periods. The posting date's own period is validated
  pre-write, `no_period` and `closed` getting different messages because the
  remedies differ.
- **`fiscal_period_id` is asserted non-null** on every journal before it is
  recorded. `createJournalEntry` leaves it NULL for a date no period covers, and
  `postJournalEntry` skips its closed-period check behind `if
  (entry.fiscalPeriodId)` — so such an entry POSTS, permanently outside the trial
  balance, the VAT201 and the AFS.
- **A filed VAT period binds a line that CARRIES VAT coding.** A line with no
  `vat_type` contributes to no box and is unaffected; one that does is anchored
  to a return already sent to SARS. Per line, so one such line never costs the
  rest of the batch. 9,410 posted lines platform-wide carry a `vat_type`.
- **`is_active` is not a filter on any figure query** (it is a picker flag), but
  BOTH accounts must be active to be POSTED to — a deactivated account refuses
  every posting, so that is a request-level refusal, not a per-line skip.
- **The contra leg of an earlier reclassification is never a candidate** —
  moving it moves the correction, not the amount. Identified as
  `(journal_entry_id in reclassification_batch_lines) AND (account = that
  batch's source_account_id)`, not by a recorded line id: `createJournalEntry`
  returns no line ids and lines in one entry share a `created_at`. The TARGET leg
  IS a candidate: an amount moved onto an account may be moved on again.
- **A reversed reclassification frees its source lines again**, or a corrected
  mistake would be permanently unfixable.
- **`source` is `auto_adjustment`**, not a new value. `gl_journal_entries.source`
  is CHECK-constrained, and widening it takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and a full
  validation scan on the busiest table in the schema.
- **The impact's two sides are independently derived.** Both are full
  aggregations over the same window — the second with the moved lines projected
  onto the target — folded by the ONE owned classifier
  (`gl/accountClassification#aggregateFigures`). `after = before + delta` would be
  a tautology. The `before` side is then compared band by band against
  `financialFiguresService`, and a disagreement surfaces as the
  `basis_disagreement` warning. **That check is necessary and not sufficient:** it
  proves this query has not drifted from the owning service; nothing independent
  computes the AFTER side, so read the journals, not only the delta.
- **`universeTotal` is its own `COUNT`**, never `movable.length +
  skipped.length` — a universe synthesized from the quantities `buildEnvelope`
  checks it against cannot fail, and `scripts/ci/check-self-defining-universe.sh`
  is a blocking gate on that shape.
- **`grossMoved`/`netMoved` are DEBIT-POSITIVE raw ledger movement**;
  `account_movement` is normal-balance signed. A credit-side move therefore shows
  a negative `netMoved` against a positive movement on a revenue target.

## The caveat this module is obliged to state

On the Velocity Fibre books, 36 of the 37 unclassified expense accounts are NOT
misfiled — `COS - Direct Material - EX2001`, `COS - Sub-Contractors - EX2005`,
`Salaries & Wages - EX4000` carry the right amounts under the right names and
merely lack an `account_subtype`. Moving them onto a generic target collapses
Direct Material, Sub-Contractors and Wayleave into one line and destroys analysis
that exists today, while SETTING THE SUBTYPE achieves the reporting goal and
moves nothing.

`warnings.ts` is therefore load-bearing, not copy. `subtype_remedy_available`
fires on exactly that shape; `collapses_named_accounts` when the target already
carries value from elsewhere; `no_profit_and_loss_effect` when every band is
identical before and after — which is what the live `49775627 → 5100` move
actually is: 414 lines and R11.3m moved, no reported figure changed, and the
source account's name lost.

## A timeout test that passes in five seconds is asserting the wrong thing

`lockReclassLinesForUpdate` re-issues its own `lock_timeout` on every call. So a
test that sets `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` on its own connection and then calls the
service has that value **silently overridden**, waits the full production
timeout, and passes — with a dead line in it that reads as though it controls
the wait. That shipped here: the contention test took **5,092ms** while claiming
to assert a 300ms timeout.

Two things fix it, and both are load-bearing:

- the timeout is an **overridable parameter**, bound with
  `set_config('lock_timeout', $1, true)` because `SET LOCAL` cannot bind one and
  the literal form would mean interpolating a value into a statement;
- the test asserts **elapsed time** (`expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(2_000)`).
  Hardcoding the literal back pushes it to ~5,003ms and it goes red.

**Elapsed time is the tell.** This was the third test-that-could-not-fail found
in this module in one day, and the third found by its author rather than a
reviewer — the other two were a lock whose wiring no test observed, and a
`basisFault` that two correct implementations can never trigger.

## A second lock phase nobody orders

`lockReclassLinesForUpdate` orders its own acquisition (ascending by `id`, and
`LockRows` sits above `Sort`). It is NOT the only lock a batch takes.

`trg_gl_jl_balance_update` fires per posted line and upserts
`gl_account_balances (gl_account_id, fiscal_period_id)`, so every journal also
takes a row lock on the SOURCE balance row and then the TARGET one. Two batches
moving X→Y and Y→X concurrently in the same period would acquire those two rows
in opposite orders, which is the shape of a 40P01.

Three things about it. It is **identical under an account-level lock**, so it is
not a reason to prefer either design. It is **shared with every other posting
path** — `bulk_allocate_bank_transactions` posts 500 journals through the same
trigger. And an attempt to demonstrate it empirically was **inconclusive** (the
probe blocked rather than deadlocking, and was abandoned), so it is recorded as
reasoned-but-unproven rather than as a known defect. If it does fire, the
consequence is a clean one: 40P01 throws, the registry's savepoint unwinds,
nothing is posted, and the agent retries.

## Multi-company acceptance

Proven on three chart shapes, not one. A difference between them is not a defect
unless it is unexplained.

**No system account is resolved anywhere on this path.** 59 modules are
reachable from `post.ts` / `plan.ts` / `lineLock.ts` / `batchService.ts` and the
write tool, and `getSystemAccount` appears in none of them. That is structural
rather than lucky: a reclassification takes BOTH its accounts from the caller,
ownership-checked against `ctx.companyId`, so there is no ROLE to resolve.
Depreciation must resolve `depreciation_expense`; bank allocation resolves
`bank`; asset disposal resolves `disposal_profit_loss` — of which zero exist on
any company in any state. This tool is immune to the missing-system-account
problem by construction, and the empty-tenant run below exercises the whole plan
on a company that has no system accounts at all.

| | Velocity | Brightsphere | Empty tenant |
|---|---|---|---|
| chart | 97.6% of expense value unsubtyped | almost fully subtyped | two accounts, no lines |
| flagship move | `49775627 → 5100`, 409 of 419, R10.9m | `5100 → 5001`, 2 of 2, **R3,000** | 0 of 0 |
| journals | 200 | 1 | 0 |
| identity | holds | holds | holds |
| `basisFault` | none | none | none |

Differences from Velocity, each explained:

- **`crosses_fiscal_periods` does not fire on Brightsphere's `5100`.** Its two
  lines share one day, so there is no span to warn about. It fires on
  `34024641 Salaries & Wages`, which spans 2022-04 to 2026-07.
- **`collapses_named_accounts` fires on Brightsphere and not on Velocity's
  flagship.** `5001` already carries 26 posted lines and R574,253.66; Velocity's
  `5100` carries none. That is the warning discriminating, not disagreeing.
- **`5820 Other Expense` refuses** — deactivated, so the contra leg could not
  post. It holds R317.39, and with `5100`'s R3,000 makes up the R3,317.39 of
  unsubtyped expense on that company.
- **`34550639 Pay As You Earn` refuses as a VAT control account.** It carries
  `account_subtype = 'tax'` and FINDINGS B37 records that `'tax'` is NOT VAT —
  this is PAYE. The refusal is nonetheless correct TODAY, because
  `vatReturnService` reads `'tax'` as VAT, so a move on or off that account does
  change the VAT201. **When B37 is fixed the refusal becomes a false positive**,
  and `'tax'` must be dropped from **TWO** guards in the same PR — this module's
  is not the only one:

  | Guard | File | Branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `VAT_RETURN_SUBTYPES` | `gl/reclassification/planGuards.ts` | this one |
  | `VAT_CLASS_SUBTYPES` | `gl/accountMergeGuards.ts:155` | `mcp/r2-merge-gl-accounts` |

  Both hold `['vat_input', 'vat_output', 'tax']`, both for the same reason —
  `vatReturnService` scopes the return by
  `account_subtype IN ('vat_input','vat_output','tax')` — and both become false
  positives the moment that changes. Fixing one and not the other leaves a tool
  refusing legitimate operations on a rationale that no longer holds.
  `grep -rn "vat_output', 'tax'" src/modules/accounting/services/gl/` finds both.

### The empty tenant, and the two things it caught

`propose_reclassification` on a brand-new company:

- **no accounts at all** → refuses with the shared `NOT_FOUND`.
- **accounts but no journals and no fiscal periods** → an honest empty envelope:
  `universeTotal 0`, identity holds, no fault, no division by anything.
- **`posting_date` on a tenant with no fiscal periods** → refuses naming the
  remedy ("Create the fiscal year first"), not a `GENERIC_FAILURE`.

It caught a fabrication that was mine. The impact window fell back to
`1970-01-01` / `9999-12-31` when no candidate row supplied a date, so `as_at` on
an empty report was **a date in the year 9999** — a reporting date no reader
could act on, asserted by a report that had read nothing. It now falls back to
the caller's own bounds and then to TODAY, and `no_source_lines` says every
figure is empty because nothing was read rather than because a total came to
zero. Those are different facts and only the warning distinguishes them.

**Still outstanding and NOT this module's to fix:** `posted_through` is
`1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` on an empty tenant, from `NO_LEDGER_READ` in the
shared `postedThroughService`. That is a fabricated watermark by the same
argument as the window above. The contract is being widened to `string | null`
by the depreciation workstream, which is deleting the constant; this module
picks the fix up when it lands rather than forking the shared service.

- 2026-09-04 (review round): two HIGH defects closed. **HIGH-1**, the reversal
  pair split above — the first cut moved the reversing half of every pair whose
  other half it skipped. **HIGH-2**, no lock: two concurrent batches under
  different idempotency keys both posted. Closed with `FOR UPDATE` on the
  candidate lines following `bankTxLock.ts` — an advisory lock on the account

  onto both legs, VAT control accounts refused, the dry run giving the identical
